did_you_know.text: Elihu describes how people respond to a storm: their hearts tremble, and they are shaken by its power.
Thunder is described as a mighty voice coming from God’s mouth, followed by a rumble—a sound or roar.
The sound of the storm and the light spread beneath all the heavens, and the light reaches to the ends of the earth.
Elihu emphasizes that God’s voice performs wonders and great things that people cannot fully understand.
Snow, rain, and powerful downpours are portrayed as though God commands them to fall and act upon the earth.
Animals are described as entering places of shelter and their lairs during severe weather.
The clouds and rain may serve different purposes: discipline, affecting the earth, or showing kindness.
Elihu calls Job to listen, stand still, and consider God’s wonders, directing his attention to the natural world.
The heavens are described as a strong, shining expanse, like a cast mirror—a picture of their power and solid appearance.
The chapter presents God as all-powerful, with perfect judgment and righteousness; therefore, people are called to fear him.
